  name           = "CIS-AWSConfigChanges"
  pattern        = "{ ($.eventSource = \"config.amazonaws.com\") && (($.eventName=StopConfigurationRecorder)||($.eventName=DeleteDeliveryChannel)||($.eventName=PutDeliveryChannel)||($.eventName=PutConfigurationRecorder)) }"

    name      = "CIS-AWSConfigChanges"

    value     = "1"
  }
}
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "CIS_AWS_Config_Change_CW_Alarm" {
  alarm_name                = "CIS-3.9-AWSConfigChanges"
  comparison_operator       = "GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold"
  evaluation_periods        = "1"
  metric_name               = aws_cloudwatch_log_metric_filter.CIS_AWS_Config_Change_Metric_Filter.id

  period                    = "300"
  statistic                 = "Sum"

findings.title: Router connected directly to the global network
findings.explanation: The router interface is attached to net-COMMON_GLOBAL, which exposes it to the public NIFCLOUD network and increases its externally reachable attack surface. Attaching it to the common private network avoids direct public connectivity.

findings.title: Container has direct access to a host filesystem path
findings.explanation: The container mounts the Batch host's /tmp directory with write access, allowing the job to read or modify host files and potentially affect other workloads. Using a container-managed volume avoids direct host-path exposure.

findings.title: Container root filesystem is writable
findings.explanation: The job definition does not enable readonlyRootFilesystem, so a compromised process can modify the container filesystem. The dedicated /tmp volume can remain writable for temporary data.

findings.title: Container runs as the image default root user
findings.explanation: No user is configured, so the BusyBox container runs as root by default. This increases the impact of container compromise and is especially risky for jobs executing on shared Batch hosts.

findings.title: Overly broad S3 read access
findings.explanation: The AWS-managed AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess policy grants the role read and list permissions across all S3 resources in the account. If the role is compromised, an attacker could access sensitive data from unrelated buckets.

findings.title: Subnets are not associated with a network security group
findings.explanation: The subnet1 and subnet2 inline subnets have no network security group association, so they lack subnet-level traffic filtering and enforcement. subnet3 already uses the declared NSG.

findings.title: AWS-managed broad S3 policy attached to IAM role
findings.explanation: The AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy grants read and list access across all S3 resources rather than limiting access to specific required buckets. This violates least privilege and increases the impact if the role is assumed by an unintended principal.

findings.title: Overprivileged subscription-wide role assignment
findings.explanation: The current service principal is granted the User Access Administrator role across the entire subscription, allowing it to manage role assignments and potentially escalate privileges. The configured condition_version provides no restriction because no condition is defined.

findings.title: Activity log alert contains a contradictory resource filter
findings.explanation: The alert filters for network security group deletion events while also requiring the affected resource to be a storage account. These conditions cannot match the same event, making the security alert ineffective.

findings.title: S3 bucket policy does not enforce encrypted transport
findings.explanation: The policy does not deny requests made without TLS, allowing S3 operations to be attempted over unencrypted HTTP connections.

findings.title: Malformed S3 bucket policy
findings.explanation: The embedded policy is missing a comma between Principal and Effect, so AWS would reject the policy and its intended deny control would not be applied.

findings.title: Custom role deletion events are not detected
findings.explanation: The filter checks an unrelated protoPayload.any_other_field for DeleteRole instead of protoPayload.methodName. Consequently, deletion of a custom IAM role may not be recorded by this metric.

findings.title: Overly broad S3 read access
findings.explanation: The AWS-managed AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess policy grants the role read and list permissions across all S3 resources in the account. If the role is compromised, an attacker could access sensitive data from unrelated buckets.

findings.title: Subnets are not associated with a network security group
findings.explanation: The subnet1 and subnet2 inline subnets have no network security group association, so they lack subnet-level traffic filtering and enforcement. subnet3 already uses the declared NSG.

findings.title: AWS-managed broad S3 policy attached to IAM role
findings.explanation: The AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy grants read and list access across all S3 resources rather than limiting access to specific required buckets. This violates least privilege and increases the impact if the role is assumed by an unintended principal.

findings.title: Overprivileged subscription-wide role assignment
findings.explanation: The current service principal is granted the User Access Administrator role across the entire subscription, allowing it to manage role assignments and potentially escalate privileges. The configured condition_version provides no restriction because no condition is defined.

findings.title: Activity log alert contains a contradictory resource filter
findings.explanation: The alert filters for network security group deletion events while also requiring the affected resource to be a storage account. These conditions cannot match the same event, making the security alert ineffective.

findings.title: S3 bucket policy does not enforce encrypted transport
findings.explanation: The policy does not deny requests made without TLS, allowing S3 operations to be attempted over unencrypted HTTP connections.

findings.title: Malformed S3 bucket policy
findings.explanation: The embedded policy is missing a comma between Principal and Effect, so AWS would reject the policy and its intended deny control would not be applied.

findings.title: Custom role deletion events are not detected
findings.explanation: The filter checks an unrelated protoPayload.any_other_field for DeleteRole instead of protoPayload.methodName. Consequently, deletion of a custom IAM role may not be recorded by this metric.

findings.title: SNS Topic not encrypted

findings.title: Insufficient log retention period

findings.title: Public network exposure

findings.title: Environment variable contains sensitive data

findings.title: Target group using an unencrypted protocol

findings.title: Overly permissive 'not_actions' wildcard in role definition
findings.explanation: Using a wildcard ('*') in 'not_actions' effectively denies all actions, which can lead to unintended consequences and may block legitimate operations. This configuration should be explicitly defined to avoid overly broad restrictions.

findings.title: Use of built-in 'Guest' role in role assignment
findings.explanation: Assigning the built-in 'Guest' role can lead to excessive permissions for external users. Custom roles with least privilege should be used instead to minimize risk.

findings.title: Overly permissive IAM policy attachment
findings.explanation: Attaching the managed policy 'AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess' directly to a role can lead to excessive permissions if the role is used broadly. It is better to create a custom policy with the least privilege principle tailored to the specific needs of the role.

findings.title: Network Security Group (NSG) without rules
findings.explanation: The NSG is defined but does not have any security rules. Without rules, it does not enforce any traffic restrictions, potentially exposing resources to unwanted traffic.

findings.title: IAM role with overly permissive managed policy
findings.explanation: The IAM role is attached to the managed policy 'AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess', which grants read access to all S3 buckets in the account. This could lead to unintended data exposure if the role is compromised or misused. It is recommended to use a custom policy with least privilege access tailored to specific S3 buckets.

findings.title: Role assignment lacks condition expression

resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_metric_filter" "CIS_AWS_Config_Change_Metric_Filter" {
  name           = "CIS-AWSConfigChanges"
  pattern        = "{ ($.eventSource = \"config.amazonaws.com\") && (($.eventName=StopConfigurationRecorder)||($.eventName=DeleteDeliveryChannel)||($.eventName=PutDeliveryChannel)||($.eventName=PutConfigurationRecorder)) }"
  log_group_name = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.CIS_CloudWatch_LogsGroup.name

  metric_transformation {
    name      = "CIS-AWSConfigChanges"
    namespace = "CIS_Metric_Alarm_Namespace"
    value     = "1"
  }
}
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "CIS_AWS_Config_Change_CW_Alarm" {
  alarm_name                = "CIS-3.9-AWSConfigChanges"
  comparison_operator       = "GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold"
  evaluation_periods        = "1"
  metric_name               = aws_cloudwatch_log_metric_filter.CIS_AWS_Config_Change_Metric_Filter.id
  namespace                 = "CIS_Metric_Alarm_Namespace"
  period                    = "300"
  statistic                 = "Sum"
  threshold                 = "1"
  alarm_description         = "Monitoring changes to AWS Config configuration will help ensure sustained visibility of configuration items within the AWS account."
  alarm_actions             = [aws_sns_topic.CIS_Alerts_SNS_Topic.arn]
  insufficient_data_actions = []
}
